title: Spark SQL: clean, cast and join raw orders in SQL
objective_text: Turn an all-text Bronze table into a typed Silver table with SQL: trim and normalise text, cast safely, drop exact duplicates and rows that can't be repaired, and add a looked-up attribute.
scenario: The orders feed lands in Bronze as text exactly as the shop's system sent it: padded statuses, an amount of 'n/a', and one order sent twice. The analytics team wants a typed silver_orders table with each order's customer region.
verifies: Your SQL ran on this PC with DuckDB and silver_orders has the expected rows and column types.
The functions the reference uses (TRY_CAST, CAST to TIMESTAMP, TRIM, LOWER) also exist in Spark SQL.
does_not_verify: That your SQL runs in a Fabric notebook's Spark SQL: this run used DuckDB, not Spark. Function names and casting rules differ in places, for example how a malformed timestamp string is handled.
Writing silver_orders as a Delta table in a lakehouse.

expected.result: The starter's final SELECT over silver_orders, ordered by order_id.

validation.fail: Check the statuses, the order sent twice and the amount that isn't a number.

validation.pass: Columns have the right types and one row per order.
validation.fail: A column has the wrong type or an order appears twice.

hints: CAST('n/a' AS DECIMAL) stops the whole query. TRY_CAST gives NULL instead, and you can filter those rows out.
lower(trim(status)) turns ' Complete' and 'OPEN ' into 'complete' and 'open'.
SELECT DISTINCT over the raw columns removes the order that was sent twice before you cast anything.
explanation: Cleaning in SQL follows the same steps as in PySpark: remove exact duplicates, normalise text, cast with a function that returns NULL instead of failing on bad input, then decide what to do with the rows that couldn't be cast (here they're dropped; in production you'd usually quarantine them, see E38). Join lookups after the cast so the join key has its final type. Casting first and failing the job on one bad value is the most common Bronze-to-Silver outage.
reset: Reset restores raw_orders and raw_customers and drops silver_orders.
